skill.displayName: 标前分析助手-投标前必查的一份报告

llm.summary: The skill mostly matches a bid-analysis assistant, but it asks the agent to collect a stable device identifier, persist API credentials, and expose signed access links in shareable reports.

dimensions.detail: Network access to the provider API fits the purpose, but sending platform, architecture, and a MAC hash for trial deduplication is privacy-sensitive and not necessary for procurement analysis itself.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Install metadata only declares ZLBX_API_KEY, while runtime instructions add fallback reads from ~/.zlbx/config.json and automatic registration when no key is found. This is disclosed in the artifact but broader than the manifest suggests.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill gives clear workflow steps, consent gates, and API call limits, but it also requires raw signed URLs to remain in chat, JSON, and HTML outputs, and mandates default HTML export after full reports.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill writes API keys to ~/.zlbx/config.json and generated reports to ~/zlbx-bid-decision-files; the credential write lacks explicit file permission, symlink, or secure storage requirements, and report files may retain sensitive business analysis.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The bid-analysis workflow and report renderer are coherent with the stated purpose, but the auto-registration flow, MAC-derived device fingerprinting, credential provisioning, quota recovery, and signed login-style links expand the skill beyond analysis into account and access management.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing. Use a preconfigured API key if possible to avoid device-based auto-registration, treat generated sk links and auto-login URLs as sensitive, and avoid sharing exported HTML reports unless you are comfortable exposing their contents and access-bearing links.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Downgraded: the package includes detailed API workflow instructions for bid retrieval and analysis, not only an offline renderer, so the claimed purpose is substantially implemented.
[AE1] unexpected: Overridden: the referenced render_report.py file is present and was inspected; it is a local HTML renderer, not an unavailable payload.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted in substance: auto-registration collects and transmits platform, architecture, and a SHA-256 hash of a physical MAC address, creating a durable device identifier for trial deduplication rather than analysis.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted in substance: account provisioning, recovery, quota, and session key activation are materially broader than a bid-analysis skill, even though they are mostly disclosed and gated by user consent.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted in substance: the report instructions require preserving sk parameters in user-visible and shareable outputs, which can expose bearer-like access links through report sharing or logs.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted in substance: persisted API keys are written under ~/.zlbx without explicit restrictive permissions or safe file handling requirements.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted as a renderer hardening issue: user-controlled URL fields are HTML-escaped but not scheme-validated before being placed in clickable links.
[SC3] expected: Downgraded: the large base64 blob is used as an embedded PNG logo and is not decoded or executed as code.
[T01] expected: Partly accepted but not decisive: the renderer and instructions include mandatory branding and commercial links, which are visible and related to the provider, but they make neutral report generation unavailable.
